title: SYSK Selects: How Munchausen Syndrome Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2011 episode on Munchausen syndrome. The hosts explain factitious disorder (fabricated or induced illness), how patients feign symptoms and harm themselves, risk factors, and red flags for doctors. They cover Munchausen by internet (the Casey Swinton hoax), Munchausen syndrome by proxy (Roy Meadows' cases, David Southall's surveillance, Mary Beth Tinning, Juanita Hoyt, the SIDS connection), the controversy over the diagnosis including Asperger's by proxy claims, and William Bowles-style serial medical patient Munchausen case. The episode closes with X-Files references, Eminem's lyric, and listener mail about a marriage proposal.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces the rerun of the February 2011 episode on Munchausen syndrome. Chuck and Josh chat about nails and The Sixth Sense, then clear up the terms factitious and facetious.

segments.title: Defining Munchausen syndrome and its history
segments.summary: Munchausen is defined as faking or inducing illness to get medical care and sympathy. Munchausen by Internet is introduced. Richard Asher named the disorder in The Lancet, after Baron Munchausen. The hosts distinguish it from hypochondria and malingering and mention the film The Adventures of Baron Munchausen.

segments.title: Causes, risk factors and treatment
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the psychological basis of the disorder, including childhood loss or abuse, prolonged childhood illness, and a wish to be in medicine. They describe passive-aggressive traits and treatment approaches similar to those for depression or anxiety.

segments.title: How patients feign illness and harm themselves
segments.summary: Patients choose specific or vague symptoms, lie, and tamper with tests, such as heating thermometers, tainting urine, and injecting toxins. Doctors may spot red flags such as eagerness for tests, knowledge of hospital routines, and inconsistent medical histories.

segments.title: Pathological lying and extreme cases
segments.summary: A man who claimed bereavement and a large family was found to have lied about all of it. The hosts discuss pseudologia fantastica, suicide risk, and a man who cut himself and smeared feces on the wounds, leading to amputations.

segments.title: Munchausen syndrome by proxy
segments.summary: Roy Meadows coined Munchausen syndrome by proxy, citing cases of a poisoned child and a six-year-old with repeated infections. The hosts describe the child-protection consequences and the burden of proof on accused parents. They also discuss David Southall's covert surveillance and his controversial reinstatement.

segments.title: Mary Beth Tinning, Juanita Hoyt, and controversy
segments.summary: Mary Beth Tinning's nine children died and she was convicted in 1987. Juanita Hoyt's six children died, and her case shaped SIDS research before she was found to have killed them. The hosts discuss the Asperger's by proxy controversy and signs of Munchausen by proxy such as healthcare workers as caregivers.
topics: warning signs of Munchausen by proxy

segments.title: Notable cases and Munchausen by Internet hoax
segments.summary: William Bowles is cited as a serial hospital patient who had multiple operations. The Casey Swinton online leukemia hoax, in which the blogger was actually her mother, is described. A mother-daughter case combining both disorders is also covered.

segments.title: Pop culture references and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts mention The X-Files and Eminem's lyric about Munchausen, and point listeners to HowStuffWorks for more information.

segments.title: Listener mail: marriage proposal
segments.summary: A listener named Doug plans to propose to his girlfriend Keena on her birthday, February 2, and the hosts share it on the show.
